t: LeetCode 2137 - Pour Water Between Buckets to Make Water Levels Equal: Binary Search on the Level
o: **Understanding the problem.** We may pour arbitrary fractional amounts between buckets, but each pour of k gallons spills loss percent of k, so only k*(1 - loss/100) arrives; we must end with all buckets perfectly level, maximizing that level. Example 1 ([1,2,7], loss = 80): moving 5 gallons delivers just 1 gallon, lifting everyone to 2. Example 2 ([2,4,6], loss = 50): two transfers yield 3.5 everywhere. Example 3 needs no action and returns 3. Only aggregate arithmetic matters - which bucket feeds which is irrelevant - and with n up to 10^5 plus a 10^-5 tolerance, binary search over the answer with an O(n) feasibility probe is the intended shape.
k: Level x is achievable iff (1 - loss/100) * total surplus above x >= total deficit below x.
Surplus shrinks and deficit grows as x rises, so feasibility is monotone - ideal for binary search on the answer.
Individual pour routes are irrelevant; only aggregate volumes matter.

a.n: Approach 1: Binary Search on the Level
a.i: Guess a level x and tally surplus E = sum of (b_i - x) over buckets above x and deficit D = sum of (x - b_i) below it. Pouring from surplus regions retains fraction r = 1 - loss/100, so x works iff r*E >= D. Raising x only shrinks r*E and grows D, so the predicate flips exactly once; bisecting ~100 times pins x far tighter than the required 1e-5.
s: Set lo = 0, hi = max(buckets), r = 1 - loss/100.
Repeat about 100 times: probe mid = (lo + hi) / 2.
In one pass compute surplus (buckets above mid) and deficit (buckets at or below).
If surplus * r >= deficit, set lo = mid (feasible, aim higher); else set hi = mid.
a.t: O(100 n) - about 100 bisection probes, each an O(n) tally; fine for n <= 10^5

a.n: Approach 2: Closed Form via Sorting and Prefix Sums
a.i: Sort the buckets with prefix sums P. For a level x between b[k-1] and b[k], exactly k buckets are short: deficit = kx - P[k] and surplus = S - P[k] - (n-k)x. Solving r*surplus = deficit gives x(k + r(n-k)) = r(S - P[k]) + P[k]. The piecewise-linear balance function is continuous and strictly increasing (slope k + r(n-k) > 0 since loss <= 99), so scanning k = 0..n and testing interval containment pinpoints the unique root exactly, no iteration on precision needed.
s: Sort b and build prefix sums P; let S be the total and r = 1 - loss/100.
For each k in 0..n compute x = (r*(S - P[k]) + P[k]) / (k + r*(n - k)).
Accept the first x lying in [b[k-1], b[k]] using sentinels 0 and infinity.
Return that x as the exact balanced level.
a.t: O(n log n) - sorting dominates; the root scan is O(n)
a.sp: O(n) - sorted copy and prefix sums

w: Lead with binary search - it is robust, easily tuned to the 1e-5 tolerance, and its monotonicity argument is short; volunteer the sorted closed form as the precise O(n log n) refinement. Traps: applying retention to the wrong side (r multiplies the SURPLUS water moved, not the deficit), restricting pours to integers (fractions are explicitly allowed), and stopping bisection too early relative to the tolerance. Sanity-check against the three examples: 2, 3.5, and 3; note all-equal buckets return unchanged. Follow-ups: minimize the number of pours, per-pair loss rates (transportation-LP flavor), or a cap on total spillage.
